searchText: Does this make sense: ETH2.0 clients are light enough to run on the same machine. We can have a meta-client that assigns one master (e.g. @prylabs), the others are silent workers (they keep up w/ consensus but don't attest) If master deviates, one of the workers becomes the new master instead you can definitely do a local meta-client Wei Tang did a talk about this type of design at EDCON 2019 (in relation to eth1)

excerpts.author: 0xalizk
excerpts.content:
ETH2.0 clients are light enough to run on the same machine. We can have a meta-client that assigns one master (e.g. @prylabs), the others are silent workers (they keep up w/ consensus but don't attest)

If master deviates, one of the workers becomes the new master instead

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
you can definitely do a local meta-client

Wei Tang did a talk about this type of design at EDCON 2019 (in relation to eth1)
